title: Joining Earl McDonald's Louisville Jug Band
summary: The band picked Jones up as a dancing and singing novelty at about 18. He names members and says McDonald was the original jug blower and leader.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Um, now about 1920 is this? You were about 18, you joined the Louisville Jug Band?
Right. Uh... I came to Chicago in 1920 with the Louisville Jug Band.
Oh, with them. All right. And then you'd been rehearsing a little bit with them and had something worked out and you brought it into Chicago to sell it.
No, they saw me working around in Louisville and they picked me up and asked me if I wanted a job with them.
Oh, was this the Nose Whistle act that you were doing that they wanted?

Oh, yeah. I danced and sing all around the whole, tabbing and things. I was just, uh, one of them little boys jumping up around the street, singing and dancing, and they, they liked what I was doing. Figured I would be a great novelty with the band, so they had taken me on.
How big a group was the band when you joined them?
They had three outside of them, I said it was four. Uh-huh. Four of them.
Well, and Jasper's written down the names of some of them here. Louie Leslie, guitar. Yeah, guitar. And Earl McDonald, Jug. And it was his band. It was his band.
And you had a banjo and you didn't remember...
I can't think of the boy's name.
There were several jugs around Louisville. Now, was McDonald a pretty prominent one?
